item.title: Little Feat — Thu Sep 17, 7:30 PM — DPAC Presented by First Horizon
item.description: Playing is the joy and satisfaction of touring, but it comes with the hard part — travel, the endless miles on a bus. There’s no dodging the wear and tear, and Little Feat has been playing for quite a while. With tongue stuck somewhat in cheek, Little Feat announces “The Last Farewell Tour,” which will begin in April 2026. It’s deﬁnitely not an absolute, never-gonna-play again statement. This wind-down will take several years to accomplish, and while it does, Feat will continue to perform and record as long as they are able. It’s a retirement from the travel of touring. Little Feat began in 1969 when Frank Zappa told Lowell George he should start his own band. As Lowell happened to have a pretty small shoe size, the name became obvious. He found a partner/keyboard player in Bill Payne and a drummer in Richie Hayward. item.title: CULT YOUR NIGHT PRESENTS: A MORE PERFECT ANARCHY A Sacred Cabaret for Constitution Day — Thu Sep 17, 8:00 PM — Durty Bull Brewing Company
item.description: “The experiment remains unfinished.” For 250 years, we’ve lived inside a document written by a room full of powerful men imagining a nation into existence. Some of those ideas changed the world. Some left entire communities outside the room. Two hundred and fifty years later, we’re gathering again, not to tear the Constitution apart, but to ask: What deserves amendment now? This Constitution Day, Cult Your Night invites performers, poets, dancers, musicians, drag artists, aerialists, storytellers, comedians, ritual-makers, and glorious troublemakers to help draft the next chapter. Tonight we explore Joy as resistance, and the beautiful chaos of becoming. item.title: The Altar Within: Rest, Sound & Somatic Practice — Fri Sep 18, 6:00 PM — Yoga Off East
item.description:
This two-hour immersive class is your monthly invitation into deep rest, somatic awareness, and nervous system support. Guided by a somatic therapist, you’ll be held in a space that supports you in cultivating safety, self-awareness, and compassionate presence through restorative yoga and embodied practices. The experience weaves together gentle movement, crystal sound bowls, live music, guided group hypnotherapy, a tarot reflection corner, a collective altar, and intentional time for witnessing and connection. Through yoga, sound, and shared community, you’ll be invited to soften, reconnect with yourself, and gently process lived experiences held in the body. Designed as both a sanctuary and a practice, this class offers a felt experience of rest, presence, and self-ceremony that you can carry with you long after you leave the studio.

item.description:
“Not Unlike Sunlight”: Celebrating the Legacy of Alma Thomas and Black Artistry Though Primary and Colorstruck!
Join acclaimed writers Alexis Pauline Gumbs and Richard J. Powell for a conversation celebrating the legacy of pioneering artist Alma Thomas and the enduring influence of Black artistry. Hosted on the closing day of All American: Contemporary Perspectives from HBCU Artists, the program brings Gumbs and Powell together in celebration of their new books, Primary and Colorstruck!. In Primary, Gumbs writes as a spiritual student of Thomas, offering a poetic response to Thomas’s life and work, while Colorstruck! draws upon Powell’s expansive scholarship on color, Black art, and visual culture, with Thomas among the artists considered throughout the book. item.title: Food Prep Workshop — Mon Sep 28, 6:00 PM — Nature Research Center
item.description:
Come help the Museum’s Green Team celebrate Food Waste Prevention Week with a workshop on food prep! Take the stress out of mealtime! Learn simple, practical ways to plan your meals, organize your grocery shopping, and prep ahead—so you can spend less time wondering “What’s for dinner?” and more time enjoying meals with the people you love. Whether you’re feeding a family or just trying to make your week run smoother, you’ll leave with tools and strategies you can actually use. Participants will leave with their own silicone storage cube, that they will prep during the session! Workshop is free but registration is required. REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Swift Night Out (Charlotte) — Mon Sep 28, 6:45 PM
item.description:
Join NCWF, Mecklenburg Audubon Society, and NCWF Charlotte Wildlife Stewards Chapter to meet the most spectacular aerial insectivores, Chimney swifts. These birds spend almost their entire lives flying, hunting insects, and even bathing on the wing. Having lost much of their habitat to development, chimney swifts now rely on brick mason chimneys for survival. As the sun goes down and the swifts make their way home for the night, chat with local conservationists about chimney swift biology, behavior, and conservation. Discover their miraculous fall migration and observe swifts up close using scopes and binoculars. The night will culminate with the spectacle that is many hundreds of swifts chattering while swirling into a vortex before dropping into the chimney. Help us count the birds and contribute to their conservation efforts. REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Fri Dec 11 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Fri Dec 11, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Carolina History Tour — Fri Dec 11, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Learn more about the history of the nation’s first public university by attending a Carolina History Tour. The Carolina History Tours cover more than 200 years of the history of UNC-Chapel Hill, including the establishment of the university in the 18th century, the history of campus landmarks including the Old Well, Davie Poplar, and Unsung Founders Memorial, the push to open enrollment to all North Carolinians, and the growth of the school in the 20th and 21st centuries. Tours will begin at the Old Well and finish at Wilson Library. Most tours last a little over an hour.
Led by staff from the Wilson Special Collections Library, these tours are part of the University Library’s commitment to collecting, preserving, and sharing the history of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
Registration is required. You can register for your spot here.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill
